newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus sees boost to June qtr production.
newsitem.headline: Novus sees boost to June qtr production.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected new oilfields being brought on stream in the current quarter to offset a fall in production in the three months to end March.

March quarter prodution eased eight percent to 1.95 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), compared with the record performance in the December quarter, the company said in its quarterly report. Weaker oil prices also affected sales revenue, which fell 11 percent on the December quarter to A$29.8 million.
"Novus expects output from five new oilfields being brought into production in the current quarter to offset a small decline in production in the opening quarter of 1997," the company said.
Novus has interests in Indonesia, Australia, Pakistan, Thailand, Oman and the Philippines.
Managing director Bob Williams said the company had already replaced its expected 1996/97 production through acquisitions and discoveries.
Novus purchased part of the petroleum interests of WMC Ltd in March for A$6 million, giving it equity in six new areas in the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia.
Novus shares were trading up seven cents at A$3.95 at 1.05 p.m. (0305 GMT).
